newsitem.title: PERU: Peru presidency minister quits for personal reasons.
newsitem.headline: Peru presidency minister quits for personal reasons.

text.p: Presidency Minister Jaime Yoshiyama, a close ally of President Alberto Fujimori and one of Peru's most powerful politicians, resigned on Friday for personal reasons, Government Palace sources said.
"He met with Fujimori this afternoon to present his irrevocable resignation," one of the sources said, adding that Yoshiyama planned now to focus on private business interests.
The presidency ministry, which manages the government's social projects and controls a large proportion of the national budget, is one of the top political posts in Peru.

Yoshiyama, a former Congress president and leading member of Fujimori's New Majority-Change 90 party, was appointed presidency minister at the end of 1995 after losing an election for the Lima mayorship.
His election defeat to independent candidate Alberto Andrade was considered a political humiliation, but his career was soon revived when Fujimori named him to the cabinet.
The palace sources said no replacement for Yoshiyama had been named by late Friday. They could not confirm speculation that Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi had also resigned.
